fine_trace.note: Attacker-controlled data-segment init-expression bytes (0xFC 0x10 0x0B) from the wasm binary are captured as segment->initExpr; i_bytes points into the module byte stream.
The init-expr bytes become the wasm byte stream of a fresh M3Compilation (wasm = *io_bytes, wasmEnd = i_end), so they will be decoded as opcodes.
Invokes the block-statement compiler on the attacker-controlled expression bytes.
Reads the extended-opcode prefix 0xFC plus the sub-opcode byte 0x10, producing the 16-bit opcode 0xFC10 from attacker input.
The second byte is merged: opcode becomes 0xFC10; the low byte 0x10 is fully attacker-controlled and is not validated against the 0xFC sub-opcode table size.

Root cause: the low byte 0x10 is used directly as an index into c_operationsFC with no bounds check. c_operationsFC has only 8 entries (9 with DEBUG termination), so index 16 is out of bounds and the returned pointer points past the array.
opinfo becomes a pointer 8+ entries past the end of c_operationsFC; the opinfo == NULL check passes because the stale address is non-NULL.
Global-buffer-overflow: reads the compiler function-pointer field from memory past the end of c_operationsFC (8-byte read beyond the array), yielding garbage.
Sink: the out-of-bounds compiler pointer is invoked as a function, jumping to a garbage address and crashing (ASan SEGV / global-buffer-overflow).
